section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the sword with two edges represents the two modes of divine service—love with delights and love like fiery sparks—corresponding to Torah and prayer, which cut off the nourishment of the husks from two sources, and the superiority of prayer's upward service.
section.t: And this is the sword with two edges,
which is the matter of the service of love with delights and love like fiery sparks.
And in general, it is the difference between Torah and prayer,
for Torah is from above downward,
through which it cuts off the nourishment from the aspect of the encompassing [light],
and prayer is from below upward,
in a manner of war,
for the time of prayer is a time of battle,
and through this it cuts off the nourishment from the multitude of contractions.
And this is the sword of Havayah,
for both modes of the nourishment of the husks are cut off specifically by Havayah,
the nourishment from the aspect of the encompassing [light] is cut off by Havayah,
as it is written,
"If you elevate yourself like an eagle, from there I will bring you down, says Havayah,"
and also the nourishment from the aspect of the multitude of contractions is cut off by the name Havayah,
for the nourishment of the husks is specifically from the aspect of the multitude of contractions of the name Elokim,
and within this itself, it is not from the aspect of "Eileh,"
but rather from the aspect of "Yam,"
for from these 48 permutations the children of Cham, the earth, draw nourishment,
but from the aspect of the revelation of the name Havayah, the nourishment is nullified.
And this is the sword of Havayah,
which is a sword with two edges to cut off their nourishment in both modes.
And in [divine] service, it is the service of Torah and the service of prayer,
and there is an advantage in prayer, which is from below upward, over Torah, which is from above downward,
like the advantage of subjugation over transformation,
and like the advantage of the penitent over the righteous,
therefore Mashiach comes to bring the righteous to repentance.
And this is "whoever recites the Shema... is as if he holds a sword with two edges,"
for the Shema is called a double-edged sword to cut off the nourishment from the three ministers of Pharaoh,
through which is the exodus from Egypt,
and therefore the Shema concludes "I am Havayah your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section details the five weapons in the service of the heart—prayer: the sword corresponds to Pesukei Dezimra, the bow to the Shemoneh Esrei, the goad to constant arousal against the evil inclination, the lance to the Shema, and the shield to the wearing of tefillin.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter of the five weapons in particular in the service of the heart, which is prayer:
The sword corresponds to Pesukei Dezimra,
from the term "to cut down the arrogant,"
meaning that through contemplation on the matter of "they shall praise the name of Havayah, for He commanded and they were created,"
he cuts down the arrogant.
And the bow is Shemoneh Esrei,
as it is written,
"With my sword and with my bow,"
and it is translated "with my prayer and with my supplication,"
for the advantage of the bow is that it also acts at a distance,
and this is by drawing the string,
for the more one draws the string downward, the farther the arrow will reach,
and there is another advantage of the bow over the sword,
that it also kills an enemy who does not see him.
And so too in the service of Shemoneh Esrei,
for Shemoneh Esrei is a request,
the more one feels his lack,
then the request and the fulfillment of the request will be in greater depth,
meaning that the more he becomes embittered over his distance from G-dliness,
which is drawing the string downward more,
through this the fulfillment of the request will be in greater depth.
And furthermore,
it also kills an enemy who does not see him,
which is the matter of subtle evil,
for before prayer, "the way of a man is straight in his eyes,"
for he has not transgressed positive or negative commandments,
and especially if he has learned a little Torah and fulfills commandments, he is righteous in his own eyes,
however,
when he comes to the service of Shemoneh Esrei,
he feels that he has evil within him and regrets it,
which is the request in Shemoneh Esrei, "forgive us,"
and after Shemoneh Esrei we say "we have trespassed, we have betrayed," etc.,
in all the details of the 22 letters,
through which they extract the vitality from the 22 letters from which the husk draws nourishment,
as explained elsewhere.
And all this is because the revelation is greater,
for in Shemoneh Esrei we say "Blessed are You, Havayah,"
which is the matter of the drawing down of Havayah that is above the chain of descent,
and the drawing down is into "our God, King of the world,"
therefore, from the aspect of the abundance of light, they also remove the subtle evil,
as it is written,
"And also the hornet... a great and awesome God,"
for because He is a great God,
therefore even the subtle evil is cut off.
And "Eileh," which is a goad for prodding,
its matter in [divine] service is as our sages said,
"A person should always incite the good inclination against the evil inclination,"
and the explanation of "always" is that the root of evil and good is from the aspect of gevurot and chassadim,
and from the aspect of gevurot there must always be the matter of anger.
And the lance is the Shema,
for "Romach" [lance] is the 248 words of the Shema,
and the vav alludes to the six words of "Shema" and "Baruch Shem."
And the difference between the goad and the lance is,
that through the lance the vitality is completely removed,
unlike the goad, which is merely a strike.
And its matter in [divine] service,
for in the emotions there are two aspects,
permitted emotions and forbidden emotions,
the forbidden emotions must be utterly destroyed by the lance,
unlike the permitted emotions, which require the goad,
to strike them and use them in holiness.
And the shield, whose matter is to protect against arrows and catapults,
its matter in [divine] service is the wearing of tefillin before prayer and during prayer,
for during prayer there is an arousal of the husk to distract him from his service,
as it is brought in Tanya,
that it is like the parable of an uncircumcised one standing before him to distract him from his service,
and for this is the matter of wearing tefillin,
which become garments for the soul to protect against the arrows, etc.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that on Shabbat one does not go out with these five weapons because the war with evil is suspended, though Rabbi Eliezer considers them ornaments from the week's victories, while the Sages argue they are not ornaments due to the defilement from struggling with the vile.
section.t: And now the reason will be understood for what they said that on Shabbat a person should not go out with a sword,
for in the service of the six weekdays, the time of prayer is a time of battle to fight with the evil in his soul,
however, on Shabbat eve at dark, the evil separates from the good,
and as the statement,
"And all judgments are removed from her, and there is no dominion... and she separates,"
therefore on Shabbat the matter of the aforementioned war does not apply,
and this is what they said: a person should not go out with the aforementioned five weapons,
for on Shabbat it is not the time for the aforementioned war.
But Rabbi Eliezer says that nevertheless they are ornaments for him,
meaning that the clarifications of the six weekdays, on Shabbat they are ornaments with which to adorn oneself,
for the prayers of the weekdays ascend in the prayer of Shabbat,
and it is an adornment for the person who prevailed during the weekdays.
And the Sages say they are not ornaments,
and the proof for this,
for in the future it is written "and they shall beat their swords into plowshares,"
and if they were ornaments, they would adorn themselves with them in the future,
but they are not ornaments at all,
and on the contrary, etc.,
and the reason for this is that whoever wrestles with a filthy person becomes filthy as well,
therefore it is not an ornament at all.
